generation_review.prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid; use a coherent whole THX-type variant after comparing all four:
U+3D073. LEFT separate component: vertical stem with THREE horizontal bars; bottom only modestly longer than top (top80–90% of bottom), middle shortest. RIGHT TOP is an ancient eye-like upright enclosure: rounded left/top/bottom course, right side begins BELOW uppermost bar so there is a small OPEN GAP at upper right in coherent THX-type form. Inside upper part, a short vertical drops from top bar and forks into TWO diagonal down-left/down-right branches meeting enclosure sides. Below that Y/roof partition there are TWO interior horizontal dividers, leaving THREE white bands below the partition. Preserve upper left partition field and upper-right gap; no extra divider. TWO slender separate stems descend from enclosure bottom to mid glyph, not three. Beside those stems at LEFT is a small upright branching hand/stop-like form, with two upright prongs, a curved basal rightward arm and a short rightward middle branch. On RIGHT is a narrow sinuous curled/hooked element with open turns, following the attested upper curl and lower return. At BOTTOM are TWO fairly long near-parallel horizontal bars, each starting freely on left and joined at RIGHT by a rounded return/bend. A separate oblique curved stem crosses those two bars, continuing down-right as a long sweeping terminal; the two bars plus right bend and crossing create one small right-side white field. Keep all upper stems, side small branches and curl, both bottom bars and long bottom sweep. Do not substitute modern Chinese.

visual_review.method: white inspection composite compared against all available reference specimens
reading_criteria: Left three-bar stem retains correct bar-length ordering without overlong base.
Right top enclosure: upper Y partition, two bars below it and three lower bands; upper-right opening preserved.
Two parallel stems beneath eye, left small two-prong/branch form and right sinuous hooked course retained.
Two bottom bars joined at right and crossed by long downward-right sweep, making one small right field.
notes: Viewed all four references and enlarged forms. Native follows the coherent THX-type open upper-right eye and side-course layout.
Two short eye descenders stay separate from bottom crossing; right curl connects into the returned right end of bottom bars as attested by THX.
caveats: QJZ has distinct eye-top and contact variants; no attempt was made to hybridize those with the THX-type native form.
Fine upper-right gap and small lower field require tracking checks at heavier widths.

visual_reference_review.reviewer: independent visual structural review by stroke_font_engine
notes: All four references compared. THX-like eye construction retains the open upper-right gap, upper Y partition and two horizontal dividers, giving three closed lower bands plus the upper-left compartment.

Two eye stems descend independently; small left two-prong return and separate right S curl retain every tiny side mark and open gap. Below, two bars join on the right and a long curved sweep crosses both, ending down-right.
Left three-bar component retains modest bottom width; the two lower bars remain near-equal and eye gap stays open. Short eye stems and small left prongs must not be shortened into dots or merged.
limitations: Visual comparison against the supplied chart raster; not specialist paleographic certification.
Does not verify historical writing order, exact metrics, or final font stroke width.
Verdict applies only to the source PNG hash recorded here.
